source.title: MoE Sparsity Begets Monosemanticity: Insights into Understanding and Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Ming-Xue Tian; Qi Zhang; Xiao-Han Wang; Jia-Jun Chai; Guo-Jun Yin; Wei Lin; Cai-Lian Chen; Qi-Min Xu; Si-Yu Wang; Yi-Sen Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures expert-level monosemanticity using explanation-and-prediction scores, and tests how those scores change with MoE sparsity and measurement choices; it does not use the original neuron-level method.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports fine-tuning and benchmark results, but those evaluate its adaptation method rather than individual-neuron polysemanticity. Those results are not included as rows. Figure-only monosemanticity results are recorded only where the text describes the result.
record.test_reason: Every monosemanticity measurement scores whole MoE experts, not individual neurons. Every version of the claim is about neurons (V1 vision neurons; V2 MLP neurons; V3–V7 neurons), so these results measure a related but different construct. The sparsity manipulation (R1) also does not test V5: it changes the number of routed experts k on a fixed pretrained model, not the architecture, activation function, training or regularization. The explanation-length and evaluator results (R5–R14) concern how expert scores are measured, not whether neurons count as polysemantic. Neuron-level content is limited to qualitative examples in Appendix A.10. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MoE sparsity promotes expert-level monosemanticity, middle layers are most specialized, and experts are either domain-specific or general. They report the scores are robust to evaluator choice and that concise explanations capture expert specialization. The paraphrase omits their main applied conclusion: EDMRS expert-selective fine-tuning matches full fine-tuning in-domain while better retaining out-of-domain performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses natural-language expert explanations followed by external-model prediction of expert activation, rather than the original neuron-level analysis. It evaluates MoE experts and LDS/EMS/EDMS, and varies routing sparsity, explanation length, and evaluator choice.
record.method_sensitivity: LDS varied with explanation word limit; the paper reports consistent relative trends across evaluator choices. Expert-level LDS also varied with MoE sparsity and network depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Reducing MoE routing sparsity (raising k at inference) lowers average expert monosemanticity (LDS) across four layers of Qwen3-30B-A3B. Values are figure-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoE expert-level monosemanticity increases with routing sparsity.

fits_no_version.finding: Expert LDS rises in early layers, plateaus in middle layers and declines near the output in Qwen3-235B-A22B. Domain-specific EDMS is generally lower than general EMS, and some experts are active across multiple domains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoE expert monosemanticity varies by depth and domain; domain-specialized and polysemantic (shared) experts coexist.

fits_no_version.finding: Expert LDS profiles correlate with alternative evaluators (Spearman 0.815, 0.774) and with human judgments (0.701). Explanation word limit changes LDS only slightly (0.687–0.708).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explanation-prediction scores of expert monosemanticity are moderately robust to evaluator choice and explanation length.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026
record.problems: The core sparsity and layer results are presented as figures without numerical scores in the text. The main monosemanticity analysis is at the expert level, so it does not establish the prevalence or causes of polysemantic individual neurons. The paper describes its fine-tuning selection analysis as heuristic.
record.rows_left_out: Fine-tuning benchmark and task-performance results in Sections 5 and Appendix A.5–A.8 were not extracted because they measure the proposed adaptation strategy, not individual-neuron polysemanticity or its measurement.

untested.parts: No share of polysemantic MLP neurons is measured. Appendix A.10 gives only qualitative neuron explanations within one expert.
Superposition and feature-versus-neuron capacity are not examined.
Initialization, regularization and training noise are not examined.
No neuron-level polysemanticity under different architectures, activation functions or training. The k-variation is applied at inference and concerns experts only.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not revisited.
Explanation length and evaluator effects are measured for expert scores only, not for neuron polysemanticity. Activation-range choices are not examined.

missing.what: Qualitative neuron-level explanations inside Expert 114: neurons respond to low-level patterns (function words, numbers, symbols) while the expert is described at a higher semantic level. No share or score is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests' relation and its V5/V7 labels are rejected because every metric is at the expert level, while every claim version is about neurons. The sparsity manipulation alters routing k at inference rather than architecture or training. The core results (Figures 3–4) have no numbers in the text. The word-limit effect is small: a range of about 0.02 LDS.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure the share of transformer MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts. Its systematic analysis is at the expert level; its neuron examples are qualitative.
It varies MoE routing sparsity but does not test whether the network represents more sparse features than it has neurons, or whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity.
Initialization, regularization, training noise, and whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.

The study tests routing sparsity and expert-level monosemanticity in MoE models. It does not compare activation functions, modern convnets, or regularization, nor establish that a lower share of polysemantic neurons is achieved without a large performance loss.
It does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons to determine whether their apparently unrelated inputs share a feature or job.
The study varies explanation word limit and evaluator choice. It does not examine activation-range cutoffs.

rows.subject: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Measured layer-wise LDS while varying the number of activated experts k to vary MoE sparsity.

conditions.value: four representative layers; identities not stated
varied by changing k; evaluated k values not stated

rows.measure: Layer-wise Decoupling Score (LDS), average expert monosemanticity
rows.note: The text states that reducing sparsity consistently and substantially decreases LDS across the evaluated layers and k values; exact scores are only in the figure.
rows.check: Measures expert-level LDS (mean expert EMS), not a share of polysemantic neurons. Sparsity is varied by changing k at inference on a pretrained model, not by changing architecture or training, so it does not bear on V5. Values are figure-only and the k values are not given in the text.

rows.subject: Qwen3-235B-A22B
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed LDS profiles using GPT-4o-mini as the evaluator and compared them with original scores.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation with original LDS scores
rows.note: The authors report this as evidence of evaluator robustness.
rows.check: This is a reliability check: Spearman agreement between evaluators on expert LDS profiles. It does not measure polysemanticity, and it concerns experts, not neurons, so it does not bear on V7. Treat it as a validation of the study's own method.

rows.measure: Spearman correlation with original LDS scores
rows.note: The authors report this as evidence of evaluator robustness.
rows.check: Same as R5: an evaluator-agreement check on expert LDS, not a neuron polysemanticity measure.

rows.subject: Qwen3-235B-A22B

rows.check: Human-vs-framework agreement on expert activation judgments: a validation of the study's method, not a neuron polysemanticity result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Higher sparsity corresponded to higher expert-level LDS across the tested settings, as reported in the text (R1).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: LDS varied with explanation length; the study reports 0.7081 at 20 words, the highest tested score, and describes longer explanations as more prone to overfitting sampled examples (R8–R14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Scores showed substantial relative agreement across evaluator choices and with human judgments, so the reported sensitivity does not mean the framework's relative trends disappear when the evaluator changes (R5–R7).
